brief.title: Midterm brief: Thursday, October 29
brief.markdown:
# Midterm brief: Thursday, October 29

## Bottom line
Forecasters rate the House as leaning Democratic; all 10 House forecasters have more seats rated for Democrats, from Inside Elections' 212 D / 205 R to 230 D at The Economist, FiftyPlusOne and Silver Bulletin ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). The Senate is closer: 46 D and 44 R seats are solid or likely, with 10 competitive ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Markets price Democratic control at 92.5% for the House and 67.5% for the Senate, each up one point ([Polymarket House](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026), [Senate](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-senate-in-2026)), as of Oct 29.

## What moved
- **Forecaster updates (Oct 28):** 18 rating changes, 16 toward Republicans, after yesterday's wave toward Democrats ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). FiftyPlusOne made 12, all toward Republicans, including OH-07 and FL-22 to Tossup; Split Ticket moved MO-02 from Tossup to Lean R.
- **Senate:** RealClearPolling moved Minnesota to Lean D; The Economist moved Nebraska to Likely R; FiftyPlusOne moved the Ohio special to Tossup ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). No tracked consensus changed, and no poll average crossed a threshold.

## Races to watch today
- **Alaska Senate (Tossup):** The NYT reports Democrats secretly worked to put a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/us/politics/alaska-dan-sullivan-conspiracy-peltola.html)). Alaska's governor ordered a criminal investigation into Peltola's campaign ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/us/politics/trump-peltola-sullivan-alaska-senate.html)), and Trump called for her prosecution and removal from the ballot ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/trump-calls-for-alaska-democratic-senate-candidate-to-be-prosecuted-aec2c451?mod=rss_socialpoliticsfeed)). Average: D+0.8.
- **South Carolina Senate (Lean R):** A new poll shows the race tied, with independents shifting toward Andrews ([WCNC via Google News](https://news.google.?oc=5)). It is not in the average yet (R+1.0).
- **Texas Senate (Tossup):** The WSJ reports Hispanic voters' disillusionment with Trump has put Texas in play ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/the-hispanic-voters-who-turned-on-trump-and-put-texas-in-play-0b781386?mod=rss_socialpoliticsfeed)). Average: D+2.6.

## Early vote
These are ballots by party registration, not votes, and mail ballots have leaned Democratic since 2020.
- **North Carolina:** Through Oct 27, 1,961,167 ballots were cast, 136% of the 2022 total at the same point (1,440,100) ([NCSBE](https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/Press/2026%20General/NC%20Absentee%20Stats%20for%202026%20General/2026-10-28%20Daily%20Absentee%20Stats%20Report%20-%202026%20General.pdf)). By Oct 28 the total passed 2.1 million at D 39.8% / R 25.3%; the Democratic edge narrowed 1.1 points in a day ([NCSBE data file](https://dl.ncsbe.gov/?prefix=ENRS/2026_11_03/)).
- **Florida (Oct 28):** 3,896,546 ballots at R 40.2% / D 38.9%, against registration of R 41.5% / D 30.1% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), from Florida Division of Elections data).
- **Senate battlegrounds (Oct 28):** Arizona 1,269,928 at D 37.7% / R 38.5% (via a private compiler); Iowa 338,739 at D 48.6% / R 33.1%; Kansas 282,232 at D 44.6% / R 41.2%; Nebraska 185,194 at D 39.7% / R 43.4% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), from secretary of state data).

## What the spectrum is saying
- **Left:** Politics War Room's new episode, "Big Tent Is Back," features Mark McKinnon and David Axelrod; the feed gives only the title ([Politics War Room](https://audioboom.com/posts/8970584)).
- **Center:** Silver Bulletin weighs in on South Carolina's surprisingly close Senate race ([Silver Bulletin](https://www.natesilver.net/p/some-thoughts-on-south-carolinas)).
- **Center-right:** The Dispatch argues a blue Kansas might not be a mirage this time ([The Dispatch](https://thedispatch.com/article/kansas-senate-election-democrats-hamilton-marshall/)).
- **Right:** National Review argues the Senate will break late this year ([National Review](https://www.nationalreview.com/2026/10/the-senate-will-break-late-this-year/)). This is opinion, not reporting.

## Talking points
- Five generic ballot aggregators average D+8.5 as of Oct 27, with no update since ([Wikipedia aggregate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections#Generic_congressional_ballot_aggregate_polls)).
- NPR reports polls show support for Trump among white evangelicals has fallen sharply ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/29/nx-s1-6012410/support-for-trump-among-white-evangelicals-has-plummeted-polls-reveal)).

## Coverage note
All 25 sources reported, and early vote covered 27 states. TX-17 reappeared in the House ratings table (not tracked). Kalshi had no priced markets. Candidate parties remain unresolved for seven House races (FL-22, NV-02, NY-21, NC-11, SC-01, TX-23, TX-35).
